extracted.intended_audience: early-stage researchers/postdoctoral fellows and junior faculty considering NIH mentored K (career development) awards
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for early-career investigators on selecting the appropriate NIH mentored K (career development) award and the correct FOA version based on career stage, degree, research type, clinical-trial involvement, and eligibility limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose K award type based on career stage, degree background, and type of science
rubrics_metrics.description: Your career stage, your degree background, and the type of science proposed are factors to consider as you choose a K award type to use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide between K99/R00 (for those remaining in postdoctoral positions) and the mentored K awards (K01, K08, K23) which generally require a full-time position (most often assistant professor) by the time of award.

rubrics_metrics.name: K99/R00 eligibility and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The K99/R00 'Pathway to Independence Award' is a transition award to support individuals for 1–2 years in a mentored postdoctoral position in the K99 phase and then 3–4 years of independent research in the R00 phase (5 years total support). Applicants must have no more than 4 years of postdoctoral experience at the time of award and cannot have held an independent research position or significant NIH funding as the principal investigator. There are no citizenship requirements. Applicants must commit 75 percent effort in both phases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NCCIH will provide salary commensurate with the institution’s salary structure and up to $20,000 per year for research in the K99 phase. The total cost for the R00 phase cannot exceed $249,000 per year. Transition from the K99 to the R00 phase is dependent upon completing the K99 phase aims and obtaining an independent research position with strong institutional support (e.g., tenure-track position).

rubrics_metrics.name: K01, K08, K23 overall structure and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The K01, K08, and K23 provide up to 5 years of mentored support for research and career development at 75 percent effort and require that applicants meet U.S. citizenship requirements. Applicants cannot have had significant NIH funding as the principal investigator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These three award types are structured very similarly; when considering them, confirm citizenship eligibility and absence of significant prior NIH PI funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree eligibility differences (K01 vs K08 vs K23)
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree eligibility differs by award: K01 — terminal degree (e.g., Ph.D.); K08 — clinical degree (e.g., M.D., N.D., D.C.); K23 — clinical degree (e.g., M.D., N.D., D.C.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the award that matches your terminal/clinical degree status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salary and research support caps by award
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards have different salary and research support limits: K01 — salary for 75% effort up to $75,000/yr and $25,000/yr research support; K08 — salary up to $100,000/yr and $25,000/yr research support; K23 — salary up to $100,000/yr and $25,000/yr research support. K99 provides salary commensurate with the institution and up to $20,000/yr research in the K99 phase; R00 total cost capped at $249,000/yr.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these caps to determine feasibility and budgeting for your application and career stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research type eligibility by award
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary research types supported differ: K01 — basic or clinical research; K08 — basic or translational research; K23 — clinical (patient-oriented) research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the K award that aligns with whether your proposed research is basic, translational, clinical, or patient-oriented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose FOA version based on clinical trial involvement — 'Independent Clinical Trial Not Allowed'
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports research that does not involve leading an independent clinical trial, a clinical trial feasibility study, or an ancillary study to a clinical trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate examples include basic animal studies, observational studies, secondary data analyses, or gaining research experience in a clinical trial led by a mentor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose FOA version based on clinical trial involvement — 'Independent Clinical Trial Required'
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports applicants proposing to serve as the lead investigator of an independent clinical trial, a clinical trial feasibility study, or a separate ancillary study to an existing trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select this FOA version if you will be the lead investigator on an independent clinical trial or related feasibility/ancillary study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose FOA version based on clinical trial involvement — 'Independent Basic Experimental Study with Humans Required'
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports applicants proposing to serve as lead investigator of a new, freestanding study that meets the NIH definition of a clinical trial and meets the definition of basic research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes studies that prospectively assign human participants to experimental conditions and assess biomedical or behavioral outcomes to understand fundamental aspects of phenomena without a specific application toward processes or products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'independent' in FOA titles
rubrics_metrics.description: The word 'independent' denotes that the proposed research involves a new, freestanding study that meets the NIH definition of a clinical trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although K awards are mentored, 'independent' refers to being the lead investigator on a new clinical trial; consult the NIH comparison guide for details on which FOA version fits your study design.

rubrics_metrics.name: K99 to R00 transition requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Transition from the K99 to the R00 phase is dependent upon completing the K99 phase aims and obtaining an independent research position with strong institutional support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan K99 aims and career steps (e.g., securing a tenure-track position and institutional commitment) to enable a successful transition to the R00 phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult FOA-specific IC information and contact program staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Many NIH Institutes and Centers participate in these funding opportunities; FOAs include a 'Table of IC-Specific Information, Requirements, and Staff Contacts.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After selecting a FOA, read the IC-specific table for NCCIH priorities and requirements and consider contacting the program director (lanay.mudd@nih.gov) for advice on fit and which K to choose.
